status: G4 pilot: processed, compressed and reviewed; ships as g4-dog, in Chapters I, II, III, IV, VI, VII, VIII, IX and X (on the web in Chapters II and III only)
use: A camp dog standing by the bread oven or the field oven in the canabae's court beyond the board (Chapters I–IV, VI and VIII–X).

generator.prompt: A large Roman camp guard dog of the mid-3rd century AD standing square and alert: all four legs straight and vertical, evenly spaced, head raised and facing forward, ears half-dropped, tail hanging down, symmetrical. A heavy-boned molossian dog about 0.7 metres at the shoulder with a broad head, a short tawny-brown coat, a black muzzle and a plain leather collar. No harness, no armour, no people. Realistic proportions, anatomically accurate. Single isolated model with complete geometry from every side and a bold, solid, readable silhouette from above. No ground plane, no display plinth, no text or inscriptions, no modern objects, no fantasy elements.

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the camps in the desktop build at High
review.notes: A tawny mastiff with a black muzzle and a leather collar, as asked: 1.25 m long and 0.85 m to the top of its head. In Chapters III, VI and IX it stands by the bread oven and reads as a dog at once, though it is the smallest of the animals; in Chapter II it stands by the field oven, at the edge of what the Follow camera takes in.
